# Mehmet Yigit Turali

> Mehmet Yigit Turali (Mehmet Yiğit Turalı, M. Y. Turali) is a Ph.D. student in Electrical and Computer Engineering at the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA), advised by Prof. Vwani P. Roychowdhury. He works on LLM agents with structured memory (Generative Semantic Workspaces), deep-research agents (PANINI-DR), continual learning (PANINI, ICML 2026), and machine learning for healthcare (NeurIPS 2026).

## Quick facts

- Who is Mehmet Yigit Turali? A Ph.D. student at UCLA Electrical and Computer Engineering (since September 2024), advised by Prof. Vwani P. Roychowdhury. B.S. in Electrical and Electronics Engineering from Bilkent University (2024, Summa Cum Laude).
- What does he work on? LLM agents with structured memory, deep-research agents, multi-agent systems, continual learning, retrieval-augmented generation, and LLMs for healthcare.
- What is PANINI-DR? A multi-agent deep-research harness that separates coordination of the overall investigation from the research and verification of individual subquestions. A shared Generative Semantic Workspace records subquestions, dependencies, findings, and evidence, and a verification agent checks proposed answers against that evidence. It reaches 73.3% accuracy on BrowseComp-Plus, 16.0 points above the next-best baseline. Turali is co-first author; the paper is under review at ICLR 2027.
- What is PANINI? A non-parametric continual-learning framework that encodes documents into Generative Semantic Workspaces (entity- and event-aware networks of atomic question-answer pairs) and retrieves evidence with Reasoning Inference Chain Retrieval. It delivers competitive multi-hop QA accuracy with 2-30x fewer answer-context tokens than baselines. Accepted at ICML 2026.
- What is a Generative Semantic Workspace (GSW)? A structured memory of entity- and event-aware question-answer pairs that LLMs can reason over, used in both PANINI and PANINI-DR.

## Selected publications

- [PANINI-DR: Controlled Deep Research through Generative Semantic Workspaces](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.15208) - M. Y. Turali*, S. Rajesh*, M. E. Lorasdagi, C. Duan, K. Sharma, V. Roychowdhury. Under review at ICLR 2027. *Equal contribution. Code: https://github.com/roychowdhuryresearch/panini-dr - Project page: https://roychowdhuryresearch.github.io/PANINI-DR_Project_Page/
- [Teaching LLMs to Recommend and Defer in Underrepresented Epilepsy Care](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.31036) - S. Rajesh*, K. Sharma*, T. Monsoor, M. Y. Turali, et al. NeurIPS 2026. Code: https://github.com/roychowdhuryresearch/Manana
- [Panini: Continual Learning in Token Space via Structured Memory](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.15156) - S. Rajesh*, P. Holur*, M. Y. Turali, C. Duan, V. Roychowdhury. ICML 2026. Code: https://github.com/roychowdhuryresearch/gsw-memory
- [Time-Resolved Neuronal Network Dynamics Distinguish Pathological States in Organoid Models](https://doi.org/10.1109/ICASSP55912.2026.11461496) - C. M. McCrimmon et al., including M. Y. Turali. ICASSP 2026.
- [Customizing Open Source LLMs for Quantitative Medication Attribute Extraction across Heterogeneous EHR Systems](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.21027) - Z. Fei*, M. Y. Turali*, S. Rajesh*, et al. NeurIPS 2025 Workshop on GenAI for Health.
- Full list with journal papers: https://www.yigitturali.com/publications/
